title: No Starry Sky
subtitle: The darkness there is oppressive, the light of the stars cannot be seen on the clearest night.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: She was in the same room?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: How could it be?
Kaalaa Baunaa pinches herself to keep calm.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: I know that room well. We have searched every inch of it—Unless she was hanging on the ceiling right above us.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: But, as I said, she always finds herself the best seat.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: "To be someone who can smile knowingly at the argument made by the lecturer, knowing full well the thinking process behind, while staying close to other whispering opinions."

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: "Like a perfect observatory from which we witness the events in the universe."
The fog has lifted.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Maybe I've been in the wrong direction. She didn't make the star fall as revenge on the village.
She looks up. The sky is completely cloudless, and the stars look just like the silver sand randomly scattered into the Samudra by Vishnu.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: The sky in the Realm when we met ...
She recalls the sky in the Realm, which was like the surface of dusted glassware.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Mr. Shamane, she was not on the ceiling.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Are you taking me seriously? That was just a joke to lighten up the mood.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: But, under the ground.
Kaalaa Baunaa pulls a photo slowly from her waist. It was soaked when she was in the vat, but now it is almost dried by the bonfire.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Remember the Underground Survival Guide, where we found this photo? She's right under that house.
The street is empty. All the villagers have been evacuated. There are only Manus followers wandering about at night.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: First, to the corner ...
And the ones who have returned.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: This is crazy. It has gone beyond my imagination!

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Sorry, but you don't have to come with me.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: *sighs* Say no more on that.
The two sneak from one corner to another.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: If you don't let me see my own sister, I will be dying for answers! Who would dig a basement here?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That reminds me. Her curiosity is one of the, well, the major reason she did that.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: It's possible that she was well-prepared last time she came back to Mor Pankh. I never thought she foresaw that we would be kicked out from the project.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: And as you just deduced, she did so to see that star?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Almost 100% sure. Without me, she must have asked the Manus to support her with arcane skills.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: This way.
After avoiding the wandering Manus followers, they can almost see the entrance to the old house.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: She was extremely mentally unstable when she left me. It wouldn't take any effort if the Manus had the intention to recruit her.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Watching the meteor shower and being destroyed by it has been her plan all along.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: At this point, it is hard to say who is worse, she or we, since we have prepared to die with her evil plan. However reluctant I am to admit this, sometimes arcanists are indeed strange creatures.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Heh heh ... It's like a madhouse party! Hahaha!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: But what did you teach Matilda before we left?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That's our only chance to survive in her Realm. I came up with it when I was calculating the range of the fallen star damage.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: As I said, you are the tiger cub, trying to take a bite in the arm, even when the hunter has had you in her grip.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That method was between Kumar and me. There is another theory according to my calculation: if there are more observers, the Realm might collapse.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: It's the only theory Kumar doesn't know. At the same time, it is not yet strictly verified.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: But I have faith in that girl. She is indeed a genius.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: I hope it's not too late to make our last attempt.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Hmm, if you ask me, it's not yet the time to make that attempt.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: What?
They are only one step away from the old house.
A huge Shiva statue rises with the loud rumble.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Haha! This must be the appetizer she served us.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: *sighs* Great Shiva, I hope your fists feel as light and crispy as pani puri when they land on my body!

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: *pants* That's tough.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Hey, look over there!
The statue's attack has left a crack in the floor of the old house.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: It is empty down there.
